title: GitHub Issue graph and composed coordination views
question: How do GitHub Issues and Projects represent Spec, Task, Landmark and DQC relationships and progress without forcing a tree, confusing concept Issue closure with assessment, or inventing completion?
answer: GitHub Projects, the generated Taskboard and the generated Landmark Tracker are composed views, never authority. The Issue graph carries Spec-Task hierarchy, direct or ungrouped Tasks and overlapping Landmark and DQC membership as a graph, keeps native blocking links distinct from semantic relations and generated content distinct from human content, and never treats concept Issue closure as an assessment. Views keep exactly six implementation lanes and the eight steps Idea, Aligning, Confirmed, Mapped, Planned, Journey, Review and Verified with true fractions, denominators, provenance and explicit missing or invalid states, record their coordination snapshot, freshness and conflicts, keep Tracker and execution views separate, and invent no percentages. The six-lane board reuses S-01X.

confirmation.basis: The ownership split naming Projects, Taskboard and Tracker as composed views, and these representation requirements, are owner-accepted direction relayed as settled on 2026-10-01. Project availability and the direct-Task home are not confirmed.

expectedResult.change: Record the composed-view boundary in the proposed superseding ADR; later plan the Issue graph and view capabilities, reusing S-01X, S-001Z, S-002A and S-002B, in separately assigned Specs.

uncertainty: GitHub Projects capability is unverified: on 2026-10-01 no GitHub connector Projects route was available and the gh CLI token was invalid.
If Projects cannot be used through supported access, whether v4 may ship with the generated Taskboard and Tracker as its only composed views is an open owner decision.
The home for direct or ungrouped Tasks awaits the Director disposition recorded in the S-00O assigned capability map.
